content.text:
**Finding submitted — deviation (high severity).**

- **Issue:** § 7.2 (p0026) requires us to disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer before engaging another provider. Although not labelled "exclusivity," it functions as a right of first refusal / de facto sole-supplier lock-in binding the Customer, and adds an MFC-style disclosure duty.
- **Aggravating context:** § 2.1 imposes a USD 2M/year take-or-pay minimum, so § 7.2 practically forecloses alternative sourcing; and § 12.3 expressly records that Customer has made *no* exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment — a direct internal conflict.
- **Not flagged:** non-exclusive licence language (§ 13.1), Vendor-side ownership/remedy "exclusive" references, and forum-selection clauses; the § 12.4 non-compete/no-hire terms fall under separate rules.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** delete § 7.2, with a fallback offer of a category-limited 12-month first-look right terminating automatically on service-level or delivery failure.
